operations.name: Incoming Ring Inspection
operations.setup_note: Receive the provisionally specified annealed ring and verify material certification, incoming hardness and blank dimensions. Resolve the discrepancy between the reported hardened condition and the proposed soft incoming condition before releasing machining.

operations.name: Soft Rough Turning – First Side
operations.setup_note: Grip the incoming OD in full-contact soft jaws with the left face accessible. Establish preliminary datum A and rough the accessible bore diameters, retaining soft-finishing stock.

operations.name: Soft Rough Turning – Second Side
operations.setup_note: Reverse onto a supported expanding fixture located against preliminary A, leaving the right face and peripheral steps accessible. Rough each distinct OD separately and open the right-hand internal step.

operations.name: Soft ID and Datum-Face Turning
operations.setup_note: Hold the rough peripheral land in bored soft jaws and indicate the existing bore. Finish the soft left face and accessible bore profiles, retaining only the approved post-hardening finishing allowance.

operations.name: Soft OD and Remaining Face Turning
operations.setup_note: Locate on the soft bore and seat A against a supported mandrel stop, exposing the right side. Finish the soft OD steps, shoulder, right-hand bore step and specified edge forms before pattern machining.

operations.name: Rough Peripheral and Cam Patterns
operations.setup_note: Support A on a fixture plate, locate concentrically from the soft bore and establish a transferable fixture clock. Rough the lug, cam pattern and roller-stop notches without accepting their final datum-related positions before B is established.

operations.name: External Tooth-Form Hobbing
operations.setup_note: Locate on the soft bore against A and transfer the fixture clock using approved tooling. Provisionally hob F06 first to establish its datum-contact geometry, then F01, leaving the required flank-grinding allowance; release requires confirmation that both forms are externally hobbable.

operations.name: Tooth Lead Chamfer – First Side
operations.setup_note: Locate the soft ring from its bore and A with positive angular indexing to the established tooth pattern. Present the first specified F06 lead for its drawn chamfer.

operations.name: Tooth Lead Chamfer – Reverse Side
operations.setup_note: Reverse the ring on the indexed fixture while retaining the bore location and transferred angular reference. Present the opposite specified F06 lead without adding chamfers to uncalled edges.

operations.name: Datum-Related Soft Profile Finishing
operations.setup_note: Seat A on the supported fixture, locate the bore and clock from the approved B/C construction. Finish the lug and roller-stop pattern, semi-finish the cams for post-hardening profile grinding and machine the larger tooth-end fillets.

operations.name: Pre-Hardening Rotary Deburr
operations.setup_note: Support the fully soft-machined ring without damaging its tooth and cam profiles. Remove machining burrs and apply the general edge-break requirement before dispatch to heat treatment.

operations.name: Outside Carbonitriding and Tempering
operations.setup_note: Send the soft-machined rings in a distortion-controlled rack for the provisionally selected carbonitriding, quenching and tempering service. The vendor must determine rack loads for the 100-piece order and certify the drawing hardness and effective case depth after the agreed finishing allowance.

operations.name: Heat-Treatment Receiving Inspection
operations.setup_note: Receive the hardened lot with traceable supplier metallurgical results and inspect for damage and distortion. Verify surface hardness of 700–800 HV10 and effective case depth of 0.5–0.8 mm at the specified 550 HV criterion without substituting another part's limits.

operations.name: OD and ID Ovality Correction
operations.setup_note: Support the hardened ring on the ovality fixture and measure the relevant OD and ID lands before hard turning. Correct only where necessary under an approved limit that protects the case-hardened ring from cracking.

operations.name: Hard Turning – Datum Face and Bores
operations.setup_note: Grip a supported peripheral land in low-force conforming jaws and indicate the existing bore and clocking features. Restore A first, then hard-finish the accessible bore diameters while preserving the required remaining case depth.

operations.name: Hardened Cam Profile Grinding
operations.setup_note: Locate on the hard-finished bore against A and index using the approved B/C construction in a dedicated contour-grinding fixture. Grind the 20 cam profiles to the specified contour, straightness and finish while maintaining the defined ramp intersection.

operations.name: Hard Turning – Remaining Diameters and Face
operations.setup_note: Reverse onto a segmented mandrel located from the final bore and A, with relieved support that does not contact the finished cams. Hard-finish the remaining diameters, right face, shoulder and specified groove before tooth grinding.

operations.name: External Tooth-Form Grinding
operations.setup_note: Locate the hardened ring from the final bore and A, clocking to the approved datum construction. Grind the previously hobbed external forms with qualified tooling while preserving their specified leads and root radii.

operations.name: Laser Traceability Marking
operations.setup_note: Support the finished ring in a non-marring nest and expose the customer-approved marking location. Laser-mark YYMMDDXXXX using the specified 5 mm text size without encroaching on functional surfaces.

operations.name: Final Dimensional and Profile Inspection
operations.setup_note: Locate the finished ring in an inspection fixture reproducing the approved A/B/C datum construction. Verify the bores, face relationships, tooth forms, lug and notch positions, cam geometry and specified surface finishes using qualified gauges and profile measurement.

operations.name: Magnetic Particle Inspection and Demagnetizing
operations.setup_note: Support the hardened ring on the MPI bench and inspect the functional profiles for cracks under the approved inspection procedure. Demagnetize after inspection and verify residual magnetism against the drawing maximum of 5 A/cm.

operations.name: Safe-Launch Inspection
operations.setup_note: Present the accepted rings to the dedicated safe-launch inspection station with individual traceability. Apply the retrieved control-plan requirement for 100 percent checking of critical characteristics during the first three months of supply.

operations.name: Final Washing
operations.setup_note: Rack the accepted rings so the interrupted bores, cam ramps and roller-stop notches drain freely. Wash after final inspection, MPI and safe launch, splitting the 100-piece order into validated washer loads as necessary.

operations.name: Cleanliness Acceptance
operations.setup_note: Handle washed rings with clean gloves in a controlled inspection area. Verify cleanliness class SKK 2D and contaminant mass not exceeding 1 mg per piece using the customer-approved assessment method and sampling plan.

operations.name: Rust Prevention and Packing
operations.setup_note: Transfer accepted clean rings into the preservation and packing station without contaminating functional profiles. Apply the approved cleanliness-compatible rust preventive and segregated protective packaging.

operations.name: Dock Audit and Dispatch Release
operations.setup_note: Present the packed lot with inspection, heat-treatment and traceability records at the dispatch inspection station. Complete the dock audit and then authorize shipment without further machining or unpacking of accepted units.

clarifications.question: Is the incoming ring to be supplied annealed rather than in the reported quenched-and-tempered condition?
clarifications.suggested_default: Purchase a certified annealed ring and interpret the reported 700 HV10 condition as the finished-part requirement.

clarifications.question: Is carbonitriding approved to satisfy the drawing's case-hardening requirement?
clarifications.suggested_default: Use the retrieved outside-carbonitriding control route only after approval, meeting the drawing hardness and case depth.

clarifications.question: What is the controlling tooth-form definition for F01?
clarifications.suggested_default: Provisionally treat F01 as an external hobbable and grindable tooth form; do not release tooling or production without its approved definition.

clarifications.question: What is the controlling tooth-form definition for F06?
clarifications.suggested_default: Provisionally treat F06 as an external hobbable and grindable segmented form; revise the route if it is instead an internal or non-generating engagement profile.

clarifications.question: Which physical contact surface on F06 establishes planar datum B?
clarifications.suggested_default: Use a designated planar contact on F06 only after the datum target is identified on the approved drawing.

clarifications.question: How is the datum C reference line F31 constructed from the physical part?
clarifications.suggested_default: Treat C as a derived clocking reference, not an additional machined feature; hold production until its construction is defined.

clarifications.question: What is the finished diameter of F05?
What is the finished diameter of the inner base surface F17?
clarifications.suggested_default: Do not release the proposed blank bore until F17 confirms that sufficient stock remains.

clarifications.question: What is the finished diameter of the bottom flange step F28?
Can you supply the controlling cam contour for F29?
clarifications.suggested_default: Use an approved CAD contour that defines the ramp-to-counter-ramp intersection; do not reconstruct the profile from the envelope.

clarifications.question: Can you supply the controlling roller-stop notch contour for F35?
clarifications.suggested_default: Retain the 20-instance pattern but do not infer notch width or depth from the reference diameter.

clarifications.question: What is the radial depth of groove F22?
Where is the required YYMMDDXXXX marking permitted on the part?
clarifications.suggested_default: Use a customer-approved nonfunctional area with clearance for 5 mm text.

clarifications.question: Does the 1 mg per piece contaminant limit apply before or after rust-preventive application?
clarifications.suggested_default: Assess particulate cleanliness after final washing and use an approved compatible preservative that does not invalidate that acceptance.

assumptions.text: The reported quenched-and-tempered condition and 700 HV10 describe the finished part, not the incoming blank. This provisional route starts with a bought annealed ring; customer confirmation is required before stock purchase or machining.

Provisional blank dimensions are OD 197 mm, ID 152.6 mm and width 17.8 mm, providing 1 mm radial and per-face allowance against the known envelope and F33 bore. The missing F17 diameter and unresolved revolved profile may require a smaller incoming bore or revised blank.

The retrieved carbonitrided-ring sequence is used alone for the principal route. Carbonitriding, quenching and tempering are an integrated outside service, conditional on approval against the drawing's generic case-hardening callout; no induction-hardening substitution is made.

F01 and F06 are provisionally treated as externally hobbable tooth forms because they are identified as peripheral tooth rings. Their absent gear specifications are a production blocker, not permission to invent module, pressure angle or profile; non-hobbable forms require rerouting.

The special route's ISO 1328 class 10 hobbing and grinding requirement is provisional for confirmed gear forms. The generic external-sheet class 9 is not overlaid, and no gear class is inferred from the drawing itself.

Ring-blank cold rolling, coiling, welding, normalizing, blasting and sizing are omitted because the selected stock is a bought annealed ring. Internal shaping and induction-route steps are not applicable to the provisional external, case-hardened-ring interpretation.

All applicable retrieved carbonitrided-route steps are retained, including four separate soft-turning setups, pre-heat-treatment deburring, receiving inspection, ovality correction, two hard-turning setups, tooth grinding, safe launch, washing, dock audit and dispatch. The template's optional bore groove is omitted because no separate bore groove is identified; F36 is explicitly produced as a radiused ID form.

F04, F43 and F45 share the supplied provisional 187.2 mm diameter and can use one same-diameter sub-operation per setup. Unknown diameters F05, F17 and F28 remain separate; supplied assumed diameters for F03, F04, F41, F43, F45 and F48 require validation against the controlling drawing or model.

The provisional access model places F33, F17 and F48 on the first-side boring approach and F42 on the reverse approach. F18 is treated as a turned shoulder face; F13–F16 and F27 are treated as accessible turned edge forms, while F26 is the radius belonging to groove F22.

Untoleranced small shoulder radii are produced incidentally by matched turning or profile tools. Independently toleranced edge forms have dedicated sub-operations; the larger repeated F09 fillets are milled separately, and F36 receives a dedicated ID-forming operation.

Hard boring is provisionally capable of F33's 0.05 mm diameter band and Ra 0.5 µm with qualified tooling on its interrupted segments. No bore honing, OD grinding or face grinding is added; failure to qualify hard boring requires a reviewed finishing-route change.

F29 requires dedicated post-hardening contour grinding because of its 0.025 mm straightness and 0.08 mm profile controls. The listed profile-grinding capability is assumed to accept a qualified indexed fixture and suitable wheel access; subsequent hard-turning workholding must avoid the finished cams.

Soft dimensions and pre-hardening edge forms must compensate for the approved final hard-turning and grinding allowances. Those allowances must preserve the drawing case depth after finishing; the 1 mm raw-stock allowance is not a post-hardening removal allowance.
No hardness conversion to HRC is assumed. Hardness remains controlled in the drawing's HV units, and every operation from heat treatment onward is classified hardened.

F30, F31, F32, F37 and F38 are measurement or construction references, not additional components or machined features. Inspection, heat treatment, marking, cleaning and preservation therefore use empty target lists where no physical feature ID represents the result.

The heat-treatment supplier provides traceable metallurgical testing reports for case depth and hardness as part of the outside service. Numeric requirements belonging to the library's example part are not transferred to ASD 24012; the drawing's hardness, case depth, residual magnetism and cleanliness requirements govern.

There is one rotary-deburring operation before heat treatment and none after hard finishing, as required by the retrieved route. Final machining must be qualified to leave acceptable edges without a second deburring operation; washing remains after MPI and safe-launch inspection.
